correctness.rationale: Fourier basis frequencies form disjoint b-adic chains with Koopman operator pS+qS*, acting on the centered-coordinate Fourier vector v=(1,r,r^2,...) with r=1/b, so C_n=(1-r^2)/12 <v,Q^n v>. A direct half-line resolvent recurrence yields h(z)=2/(1+sqrt(1-4pq z^2)), a(z)=p z h(z), and the stated rational quotient generating series. Replacing p by q transposes the real operator, leaving each quadratic form equal; all coefficients are nonnegative. Monotone z->1 evaluation yields the exact summable maximum cusp with max(p,q). The reflected binomial-path kernel gives the critical n^-3/2 term and even/odd amplitude through the weighted parity sum; for p=1/2+u/sqrt(n), (4pq)^(n/2)->e^(-2u^2), while geometric tails and local central-binomial asymptotics justify summation. I read full RESULT.md and checker.py, checked independent finite chain symmetry and large-n constants; finite comparisons alone do not establish the limiting law. Endpoint p=0,1 is handled in formal expansions.
